population: ExtractBench development subset: first 16 short + 4 medium documents in docextract-dev/1 hash order (seen during development)
hardware: Kaggle, one T4 per arm, vLLM 0.30.0, float16
protocol: cited-values/2 prompt; max_window_chars 24000; max_schema_chars 24000; max_new_tokens 6144; OCR docTR db_resnet50+crnn_vgg16_bn

throughput.largest_document_share_of_a_input: b80b9d1450927196 (29 scanned pages, 155K-token schema in 22 groups): 136 requests, 1.73M input tokens (84%)
throughput.engine: about 300 prompt tokens/s per T4 overall; KV cache 93-100% full with about 6-7 running requests; prefix-cache hit rate about 1-2% (vLLM prefix caching is unreliable for the Qwen3.5 hybrid architecture)

findings: Accuracy of the two models is tied (0.573 vs 0.575 value F1); per-document differences are large in both directions and several come from documents unfinished at the deadline.
Prompt reading dominates: median 14.9K input tokens versus 24 output tokens per request (Qwen).
Scanned forms lose most points to values assigned to the wrong field and to check-box states; OCR text loses the box layout.
Null versus omitted made no difference: these schemas declare default null, which the scorer applies to missing keys.
model_selected: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B for further development (tied accuracy, shorter outputs, no template overhead, MTP head)
